children: iPhone manufacturer Apple Inc (AAPL, Financials) is reporting increased early interest in the iPhone 18, but a KeyBanc survey predicts demand may weaken after the enthusiast crowd is satiated.
That's up from 17% for the iPhone 17 a year ago, and almost 20% indicated they'd already bought or pre-ordered an iPhone 18. The difficulty is what happens next.
Only 41% stated they would be inclined to upgrade in the following year, down from 48% in the previous study. Price concerns were a big issue. There is one offset .
Shifts to higher priced Pro versions by consumers might help raise average selling prices even if unit growth slows.
AI is less promising than thought. Only 33% indicated AI features would motivate an upgrade, down from 42% while 65% stated they would not pay a monthly charge for AI features.
Apple's price of around 40 times 2027 profits is excessive, KeyBanc said in maintaining its Underweight rating.
The next thing to examine is whether the mix of higher-end models can make up for lower upgrade numbers.

title: Apple Is Winning on Price, Not Units, KeyBanc Survey Suggests
